title: Precise satellite clock offset estimation enhanced by regional CORS stations
excerpt:
To address the insufficient regional resolution of global station networks in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) precise satellite clock estimation and the lack of strong global datum constraints in individual regional Continuously Operating Reference Stations (CORS) networks, this study proposes an enhanced precise satellite clock estimation method that integrates global International GNSS Service (IGS) stations with regional CORS stations.

Based on the undifferenced ionosphere-free combined observation model for multi-GNSS, a parameterized estimation framework for satellite clock is established. Station selection is then performed using a comprehensive weighted scoring method, the DBSCAN clustering algorithm, and a greedy optimization algorithm. Furthermore, the Sherman–Morrison–Woodbury formula is employed to achieve rapid incremental computation of the Geometric Dilution of Precision (GDOP). Experiments were conducted using data from 30 European CORS stations and Global Multi-GNSS Experiment (MGEX) stations in May 2024.

The results demonstrate that using only regional CORS stations for independent estimation,the satellite clock estimation accuracy is relatively low, and some BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellite cannot be stably estimated. title: Maladaptive cognitive entrenchment: a neurobiological model of chronic occupational stress adaptation in healthcare clinicians and targeted neuroplasticity interventions
excerpt:
Despite epidemic rates of burnout among healthcare clinicians and substantial investment in intervention programs, outcomes remain modest and transient. title: Marking an informational text as AI-generated does not influence its ratings, study finds
excerpt:
An online experiment conducted in Germany found that labeling a short nutrition text as written by artificial intelligence did not meaningfully change how participants rated it. However, many participants did not notice the label: only about 42% of those who read the AI-labeled text reported that a source had been mentioned. The paper was published in Applied Psychology: Health and Well-Being .

Since the release of ChatGPT in 2022, artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots have become increasingly popular, with growing numbers of people using them for everyday tasks and information seeking. Although most users turn to AI for writing, education, and general inquiries, a smaller but growing proportion seek health-related information and advice.

AI chatbots have the potential to improve public health communication by providing accessible explanations of scientific findings, summarizing medical guidelines, and correcting misinformation. However, research suggests that AI-generated health and nutrition advice is not always accurate, raising questions about whether people should trust and follow such recommendations. Previous studies have produced inconsistent findings, with some reporting lower trust in AI-generated advice and others finding that people evaluate AI-generated information as favorably as human-generated content…
